title: I Let the Call-Center Script Catch the Supervisor's Cousin

parts.text: I read the refusal script to a caller who turned out to be my supervisor's cousin. I am twenty-three, first office job, headset that pinches. The script said no retro coupons after 48 hours. The cousin, Amber, wanted a month-old code. My supervisor, Rhea, stood behind me, cinnamon gum. The cubicle fabric smelled like dust and other people's lunches. Amber said, "Put your supervisor on" I said, "The script says I can't override after 48" The queue timer blinked red. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Rhea is behind me with cinnamon gum, and Amber is demanding an override the script forbids.

parts.text: I transferred because the script also says transfer if asked twice. Rhea took the call and overrode it, then later wrote me up for 'tone.' I forwarded the recorded line, which we all consent to on login, to HR with the script page. The write-up died. Amber got her coupon. Rhea got a note about related-party overrides. The headset still pinches. I bought a cheap cushion for it. Cinnamon gum still means danger in my body, which is funny. I apply for other jobs on my phone in the bathroom like a cliche that works. Scripts are only holy when they save you. HR said, "Is this a related party" Rhea said, "She's just a customer" A coworker mouthed 'cousin?' I nodded. The dust stayed. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i.
